							Zelenskyy suspends prosecutor general who charged the bureau probing his own office

articles.title: Gulf states postpone strait of Hormuz talks with Iran as Yemen conflict intensifies
articles.body:
Gulf states have postponed a critical meeting with Iran on the future of the strait of Hormuz owing to a lack of Arab consensus and growing Saudi Arabian anger with Tehran for helping the Houthis loosen Riyadh’s grip in Yemen.
The stalemate over the vital waterway came as Houthi rebels launched a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets. A Houthi military spokesperson claimed its forces had attacked the King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait, hitting fighter-jet hangars, radar systems, runways and landing strips, ammunition depots and additional targets.
Last week, Tehran-backed militias in Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to close a critical east-west pipeline that had been acting as a means for Riyadh to export oil after Iran effectively closed the strait of Hormuz.
The closure of the pipeline, the postponement of the Hormuz meeting, and the Houthis’ seizure last week of Yemen’s Red Sea coast – which gave the group control over another vital waterway, the Bab al-Mandab strait – combined to drive up oil prices above $108 a barrel on Monday.
Also on Monday, the Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince, Mohammed bin Salman, held urgent discussions with the US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper in Jeddah to discuss “the latest developments in the region”, according to Saudi media. Sources told US media last week that the Saudi de facto ruler had sought military assistance from Donald Trump to help fight the Houthis. So far the US has provided only logistical and intelligence backing,
The Gulf Cooperation Council-Iran meeting was postponed at the last minute, deferring a proposed agreement on a new temporary route for commercial shipping when the strait of Hormuz is reopened.
In a statement, Oman’s foreign minister, Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, said the meeting had been delayed in the interests of consensus. “We remain committed to fostering dialogue that supports stability and lasting co-operation in our region,” he wrote on X. He gave no further details.
The meeting would not have led to the immediate opening of the strait, since Tehran has set a series of other preconditions: including requiring the US to lift a blockade of Iran’s oil ports, the handing over of many frozen Iranian assets and a ceasefire in Lebanon.
But it would have been the first meeting between Iran and the main GCC member countries for two years. The planned agreement on a temporary route for ships to use would have formalised Iran’s control of the strait, since the entry route would have been entirely in Iranian waters.
Washington has not expressed publicly an opinion over the proposed deal, and some of Trump’s recent social media posts – claiming full US control of the strait – seemed to bear little relationship with what shipping companies have been reporting.
The atmosphere surrounding the meeting, in preparation for weeks, had been rapidly souring because of the advance by the Houthis in Yemen and the drone attack on the Saudi pipeline by an Iran-backed Shia militia in Iraq.
Vantor Technologies released high-resolution satellite images showing the damage to the east-west pipeline pumping station near Al Mesba’ah, Saudi Arabia. The station appears to be almost completely destroyed.
Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson denied any Iranian involvement in the pipeline attack, or on events in Yemen.
US military bases throughout the Gulf have been attacked by Iran in response to the Iran war.
Saudi Arabia, which backs the UN-recognised Yemeni government based in Aden, is trying to regain the initiative after Houthi forces swept down the west coast of Yemen from the port of Hodeidah last week and seized the Bab al-Mandab strait, a narrow waterway that links the Red Sea with Asia and is viewed as second in strategic importance to the strait of Hormuz.
It was claimed that a Saudi air bombardment was making it difficult for the Houthis to gain full control of the Yemen waterway or the strategic islands in the Red Sea.
The Houthi leadership says is not seeking to block all commercial shipping in the Red Sea but only Saudi-linked ships. It is also offering cut-price fees in the ports it controls on the west coast of Yemen in an effort to lure traffic away from the ports controlled by the Aden-based government in the south.
It is widely accepted that Iran backs the Houthis, but the group also operates independently of Tehran. The rebels ultimate aim is to oust Saudi Arabia from the country, and take full control of the territory.
Saudi Arabia has tried different tactics in handling the Houthis during the decade-long civil war in Yemen, including making concessions in the hope the highly ideological group would reach a power-sharing deal.
The Yemen government said preliminary tolls indicated that 150 civilians had been killed and 200 others injured in the course of the recent Houthi advance. About 85,000 people have been displaced, according to the UN.

articles.title: Finland does not intend to host nuclear weapons in peacetime — president
articles.body:
STOCKHOLM, September 14. /TASS/. Despite joining the French initiative on advanced nuclear deterrence, Finland does not intend to host nuclear weapons President Alexander Stubb has said.
"The French initiative does not replace or overlap with NATO's nuclear deterrence. Finland's primary objective is to act as part of NATO and the European Union. Finland does not intend to let nuclear weapons be deployed on its territory in peacetime," he wrote on the social network X.
Earlier on Monday, Finland decided to join the project promoted by France known as forward nuclear deterrence. As Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen has stated, the French initiative does not entail NATO-style collective defense obligations for participating countries.

articles.title: National Guard says it destroys Russian Tor-M1 air defense system worth $25 mln
articles.body:
Operators from the Black Sky unmanned aerial vehicle battalion of the Spartan brigade destroyed a Russian Tor-M1 anti-aircraft missile system valued at approximately $25 million, which the enemy had deployed deep in the rear near the occupied town of Vuhledar, commander of the Ukrainian National Guard Oleksandr Pivnenko said.
"Operators of the Black Sky unmanned aerial vehicle battalion of the Spartan brigade detected and destroyed a Tor-M1 anti-aircraft missile system that the enemy had deployed deep in the rear, near the occupied town of Vuhledar," Pivnenko said on Telegram on Monday.
According to him, the destroyed system is valued at approximately $25 million.
Tor-M1 is a mobile air defense system designed to protect troops and critical infrastructure from aircraft, missiles, and drones.
Pivnenko said the Russian military has been using such anti-aircraft missile systems in the war against Ukraine since 2014.

articles.title: Russia wanted to cow Ukraine allies with railway drone attack, says top EU diplomat
articles.body:
Russia’s Sunday morning drone strike on a Warsaw-bound train near the Ukraine-Poland border was intended to push Western countries to stop their backing for Kyiv, the EU’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday.
“This is clearly intended to frighten Western countries into ceasing their support for Ukraine, into refraining from going there to demonstrate their support,” Kallas told reporters after landing in Finland for an Arctic summit.
Kallas’ words were echoed by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, who said the strikes were designed “to intimidate Europeans, discourage them and above all to divide them.”
Advertisement
The drone hit the locomotive of a passenger train two kilometers from the frontier in Volyn region, Ukraine’s state rail operator confirmed.
Nobody was injured in the attack, but it happened shortly after a train carrying prominent Western officials and advisers had passed along the same line — prompting concerns that the diplomatic train may have been the real target.
Ukraine’s rail operator said it is “quite likely that the target of this Russian drone could also have been the diplomatic train.” Passengers included former U.K. Prime Minister Boris Johnson, former CIA chief David Petraeus and U.K. National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell.
The Russian defense ministry said in a statement that it had struck railway infrastructure in western Ukraine used to “transport military cargo” from Europe.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha responded to Sunday’s border strikes with a post on X stating that Russian President Vladimir Putin’s forces are “knocking directly on the doors of the EU and NATO,” and urged Ukraine’s allies to “throw the full weight of your sanctions at Putin’s aggressive regime.”
Earlier this month, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned of upcoming threats to Europe’s borders following a Russian strike at a Moldova-Ukraine border crossing that killed two people.
“As you know, Russia has already resorted to provocative attacks on border crossings — for instance, in Moldova. We expect similar actions targeting border crossings with Ukraine in other countries, including Poland,” said Tusk.

articles.title: Katz says Lebanon's Ali al-Taher part of Israel-controlled zone
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Katz declares Ali al-Taher part of Israeli-controlled zone as attacks on Lebanon continue
Israeli forces opened fire on several people in southern Lebanon on Monday, damaging a municipal vehicle, as attacks continued across the region and Israel's defence minister declared a strategic ridge would become part of its so-called security zone.
The shooting took place near a landfill in Chaqra, in Bint Jbeil district, as Israeli military vehicles moved towards Wadi Slouki between Chaqra and the occupied border village of Meis al-Jabal. No injuries were reported.
Israeli forces also carried out an explosion in Bint Jbeil and earthworks in Mansouri, while artillery fire targeted Mansouri, Nabatiyeh al-Fawqa, Kfar Tebnit and Arnoun, the report said.
The latest attacks came after an Israeli patrol questioned the mayor of Kfar Shuba and confiscated his phone before releasing him.
Kfar Shuba municipality said mayor Qassem al-Qadri was questioned while visiting a water tank serving the town. He was later released and returned to his family.
The incident came as Israeli forces continued attacks and demolitions across southern Lebanon despite a truce agreement and ongoing US-mediated efforts to secure an Israeli withdrawal.
Israel declares strategic ridge part of security zone
Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge would now be part of what Israel calls its "Yellow Line" and security zone in Lebanon.
Last week, Israeli forces detonated what they said were tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, a strategic highland long used by Hezbollah. The explosion was recorded as equivalent to a 4.1-magnitude earthquake.
Katz said Israeli forces would prevent Hezbollah or anyone else from returning to the area and warned that anyone approaching Ali al-Taher would be killed.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu and I have repeatedly made clear that we will not leave the security belt, and that the army will not withdraw or redeploy until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon," Katz said.
The declaration came as Israel continued to maintain troops inside southern Lebanon and carry out airstrikes, artillery fire and demolitions in areas where residents are attempting to return.
Israeli forces had been systematically targeting Mansouri, a village in the Tyre district divided by the "Yellow Line", because Israel fears Hezbollah could reposition there.
On Monday, heavy gunfire was also reported around Shaqra and Baraachit as Israeli forces sought to prevent residents from returning, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency.
The violence has raised fears in Lebanon that Nabatiyeh and surrounding areas could face a similar fate to parts of southern Lebanon that remain under Israeli occupation. Ali al-Taher overlooks Nabatiyeh and provides Israeli forces with a strategic position over the city and surrounding areas.
Talks planned as attacks continue
The latest escalation comes as Lebanon and Israel prepare for another round of US-mediated talks.
The US embassy in Beirut said Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors will meet in Washington next week to discuss implementation of the trilateral framework, while the next round of formal Lebanese-Israeli talks will be held in Rome in October.
A US State Department official also confirmed to Reuters that the Rome talks would take place in October. The seventh round of negotiations in Rome in August ended without a breakthrough on key territorial issues.
The announcement came a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said there were currently no new negotiations with Israel.
The talks are being planned while Israeli forces continue attacks across southern Lebanon, including airstrikes, artillery fire and the demolition of homes.
The Lebanese army said Israeli forces had failed to comply with the agreement, recording around 7,700 violations from the signing of the framework on 26 June last year. It also said Israeli forces had fired near army personnel and patrols.
Israel's offensive in Lebanon has killed more than 4,300 people since 2 March, according to Lebanese figures, while hundreds of thousands have been displaced.

articles.title: Finland says joining French initiative on European nuclear deterrence
articles.body:
Burak Bir
14 September 2026•Update: 14 September 2026
Finland has decided to join France’s nuclear deterrence initiative which is significant for security in Europe, the Nordic country's defense ministry said Monday.
"The initiative is a form of bilateral cooperation between Finland and France," the ministry said in a statement, mentioning that both countries have been discussing the initiative both at the highest political level and at the level of officials.
In March 2026, French President Emmanuel Macron launched an initiative on the European dimension of France’s nuclear deterrence. Eight countries were then announced having joined the initiative, followed by Norway at a later stage.
"The French initiative will strengthen Europe’s increasingly active approach to defence. Its objective is to reinforce security and deterrence across Europe," said Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen.
Stressing that the French initiative does not replace or overlap with NATO’s nuclear deterrence, the statement recalled that NATO’s nuclear deterrence is based on nuclear-sharing arrangements and relies on the US' extended deterrent.
"It is ultimately the supreme guarantee of the security of the Alliance," it added.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb also confirmed that the initiative does not replace NATO's deterrence, adding that Finland's primary starting point is to act as part of NATO and the EU.
"Finland does not intend to station nuclear weapons on its territory in peacetime," he said.

articles.title: Estonia discusses joining French 'forward nuclear deterrence' project, prime minister says
articles.body:
PARIS, September 14. /TASS/. Estonia is in talks with France about joining Paris’ initiative on so-called forward nuclear deterrence, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal told AFP.
Michal said that this was not an initiative that countries could simply join, as it required certain capabilities and a certain level of readiness. He noted that France was also helping ensure Estonia’s independence by deploying its troops there. He added that if nuclear cooperation could be deepened, it probably would be, and that Estonia was already under NATO’s nuclear umbrella.
Earlier on Monday, Finland decided to join the so-called forward nuclear deterrence project promoted by France. Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen said that the French initiative does not impose NATO-style collective defense obligations on participating countries.
In March, French President Emmanuel Macron said that Paris planned to move toward a "forward deterrence" initiative involving joint exercises with partner countries as well as the deployment of elements of France’s strategic forces in other European countries. He also announced plans to expand the country’s nuclear arsenal, while Paris no longer plans to disclose the exact number of warheads.

articles.title: Meink Reveals Space Force Has ‘On-Orbit Space Control Weapons’
articles.body:
NATIONAL HARBOR, Md.—Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed Sept. 14 the Space Force has “space control weapons” on orbit today—the Pentagon’s most direct acknowledgement to date that the U.S. is operating offensive capabilities in space.
“Today, we continue to ensure we remain ready to meet the challenge of evolving threats wherever they exist,” Meink said during the opening keynote at AFA’s Air, Space and Cyber Conference. “This is why the Space Force now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.”
Meink’s explicit nod to U.S.-operated space weapons comes amid a concerted push to speak more openly about on-orbit threats and the Space Force’s ability to respond to them. China and Russia, in particular, continue to demonstrate aggressive maneuvers and are developing—and demonstrating—space weapons of their own. U.S. officials in recent years have discussed the need for “counter-space” capabilities and “space fires,” as well as the development of space-based interceptors designed to shoot down missile threats. And last December, President Donald Trump issued an executive order underlining the Space Force’s role in not only defending space assets, but also in the attack mission.
But Meink’s mention of existing on-orbit space weapons is a first. During a question and answer session following his speech, Meink said the acknowledgement was intentional and the phrasing “very well thought out.”
“It is critically important that we maintain our dominance, not only in the air but in space,” he said. “So, we’ve had to take steps to make sure that when we’re threatened, we can take care of that.”
Meink declined to discuss the capabilities in more detail during a briefing with reporters following his keynote—including whether the systems in question are kinetic or non-kinetic. He argued that while acknowledging the existence of U.S. space weapons in orbit may serve a deterrent function, “talking about the details of what we’re doing would actually not benefit that deterrence.”
“We’re not going to talk about the specifics of what we’re doing, whether we’ve tested, not tested, or anything else,” he said. “I would just say that the space environment is critical for military and economic security, and we need to make sure that the U.S. can operate freely there.”
Meink said the Space Force is working now to proliferate systems meant to help track and take out threats from space and highlighted two key efforts: the Space-Based Interceptor program and the Space-Based Air-Moving Target Indication constellation. Both are part of the Pentagon’s Golden Dome advanced missile defense shield.
On SBI, one of Golden Dome’s more ambitious technical lifts, Meink said the program has moved from “initial contract to flight-ready hardware” in under a year. The Space Force is leading a prize competition to evaluate the affordability and scalability of SBIs in increments and potentially field an initial capability by 2028.
Gen. Michael Guetlein, Golden Dome director, said in August the SBI contractor pool has completed the program’s first increment, called Gate One, which focused on solidifying a design and conducting component level testing. Guetlein said it appears all of the providers will move to Gate Two, where they will build a prototype. Those that progress to Gate Three must prove the capability works in space, and Gate Four providers must show their interceptors can be integrated with the broader Golden Dome architecture.
Another key Golden Dome contribution for the Space Force is its Space-Based AMTI program. While tracking airborne threats has long been a mission performed by aircraft, the Space Force is working with the National Reconnaissance Office to add satellites to the mix, with the goal of making the mission more resilient against adversaries’ anti-access/aerial denial systems.
The service awarded SpaceX a $4.2 billion contract in May to start building out the Space-Based AMTI constellation, and Meink said the first of those satellites will launch this month. The Space Force hasn’t disclosed how many spacecraft will initially launch or how many satellites the constellation will eventually feature.
“Taken together, these investments will help us adapt and scale the force for today and tomorrow’s threats,” Meink said.

articles.title: Russia loses about 1,700 troops, 74 artillery systems in past day - General Staff
articles.body:
Ukraine's Defense Forces eliminated about 1,700 occupying troops, 74 artillery systems, seven multiple rocket launchers, 2,124 operational-tactical-level drones, and 550 vehicles and pieces of special equipment over the past day, the General Staff of Ukraine's Armed Forces reported on its Telegram channel Monday morning.
"The enemy's total combat losses from February 24, 2022, to September 14, 2026, are estimated at: personnel - about 1,508,600 (+1,700); tanks - 12,345 (+1); armored combat vehicles - 25,331 (+1); artillery systems - 49,752 (+74); multiple rocket launchers - 2,127 (+7); air defense systems - 1,637 (+2); ground robotic systems - 2,615 (+12); operational-tactical-level drones - 516,441 (+2,124); vehicles and fuel tankers - 148,807 (+548); special equipment - 4,683 (+2)," the statement said.
The data is being updated.

articles.title: Russian attacks kill 6, injure 43 across Ukraine over past day, Donetsk Oblast among hardest hit
articles.body:
Russian attacks kill 6, injure 43 across Ukraine over past day, Donetsk Oblast among hardest hit
At least six people were killed and 43 others injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day, local authorities said on Sept. 14, with Donetsk Oblast among the hardest hit. The region has remained one of Russia’s main objectives since the beginning of the full-scale war and continues to be a key focus of Moscow’s war against Ukraine.
Russian attacks killed three people and injured 13 others, Donetsk Oblast Governor Vadym Filashkin said. Two people were killed in Kramatorsk and one in Druzhkivka overnight.
Russian attacks continued across the region into the morning. In Sloviansk, one person was injured. In Kramatorsk, two people were killed and 10 others injured. One person was injured in Znamenivka. Another person was injured in Spasko-Mykhailivka. One person was also killed in Druzhkivka.
Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS) also detailed the attack on Sloviansk.
"An airstrike damaged three homes. Debris and dry grass caught fire in one yard over an area of 100 square meters," the DSNS said, adding that intense drone activity disrupted firefighters' work.
The agency said two additional first-person-view (FPV) drone attacks sparked new fires, setting a car and an outbuilding ablaze.
Overall, the Air Force said Russia attacked Ukraine with 108 drones. Air defenses shot down or intercepted 85 drones, while strikes were recorded at seven locations.
Two people were killed and 14 others were injured in Russian attacks on Kherson Oblast, Governor Oleksandr Prokudin said.
One person was killed and four others were injured as Russian forces attacked Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Governor Ivan Fedorov said.
Five people, including a newborn, were injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv Oblast, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said. The overnight attack continued into the morning, when, at around 10 a.m. local time, a Russian drone struck a civilian vehicle, injuring a 62-year-old man.
In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Russian attacks injured six people, local authorities said. Four people were injured overnight, and two more people were injured in the early morning.

articles.title: Russian oligarch close to Putin reportedly paid for part of Donald Trump Jr’s lavish wedding
articles.body:
A top Democrat has demanded answers after it was reported that a Russian oligarch close to Vladimir Putin paid hundreds of thousands of dollars toward Donald Trump Jr’s wedding in the Bahamas earlier this year.
Trump Jr, the US president’s eldest child, married Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson in a lavish three-day celebration across two exclusive private islands in May, which according to ProPublica was partially bankrolled by Umar Kremlev, a member of the Russian president’s circle.
Citing records and interviews with three anonymous sources familiar with the event, ProPublica reported that Kremlev footed the bill to rent one of the islands where a reception was held and where guests slept, along with other large expenses, including a huge firework show.
“Why did a Russian oligarch close to Putin fund Trump Jr.’s wedding in the Bahamas?” posted Robert Garcia, the ranking member and lead Democrat on the House oversight committee, on social media. “Umar Kremlev spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on the President’s son. What did he get in return? We need answers.”
Kremlev has a longstanding relationship with Putin. He is the head of the International Boxing Association (IBA), a sporting body that has been backed by the state-owned Russian energy company Gazprom. According to ProPublica, the wedding payments came from an IBA-affiliated entity in Dubai that the boxing association uses for financial transactions.
In the days before the wedding party, he reportedly went to China as part of a delegation accompanying Putin, and the month prior the Russian president had bestowed him with a state honor, the Order of Friendship. The Ukrainian government has imposed sanctions on Kremlev, citing his closeness to Putin and Russian security services.
Alexander Lagutin, a businessperson who has held senior roles at a Russian defense contractor and a state-backed energy company, had been with Kremlev on the China trip. Kremlev’s right hand at the IBA, Elena Sobol, attended the wedding, too.
While the event was extravagant, the guest list was intimate, with only about 50 people attending, most of whom were immediate family, close friends and business partners of the couple. Then there was Kremlev, who reportedly didn’t attend the ceremony itself, which was limited to just 18 guests, but was present with a large contingent of Russians at the party, much to the confusion of the other guests. The group reportedly sometimes stood off by themselves speaking Russian, according to ProPublica.
The affair has raised questions about the implications of a member of Putin’s circle financially supporting and gaining such intimate access to the US president’s family. In recent years Trump Jr has emerged as a leading campaign surrogate for Trump and has even been touted as a potential political heir.
Retired FBI official Frank Montoya Jr told ProPublica: “If I’m paying for your wedding, at some point, you’re going to owe me something. This should be unthinkable for the son of the president.”
It remains unclear why Kremlev helped pay for the wedding and why he was there, when he appears to have only met Trump Jr – the executive vice-president of the Trump Organization, who has a personal net worth somewhere in the ballpark of $300m – quite recently.
Donald Trump famously didn’t attend the wedding. “He’d like me to go, but it’s going to be just a small, little private affair,” the US president told reporters a few days before the nuptials. “I said, you know, this is not good timing for me. I have a thing called Iran and other things.”
In response to detailed questions from ProPublica, a spokesperson for Trump Jr did not deny that Kremlev had helped fund the wedding. “Umar is a personal friend of Don,” the spokesperson said, adding Kremlev is “not someone he has a business relationship with” and that the men met through a mutual friend in the hunting world.
After the article was published, Bettina Trump also confirmed the report, thanking “our dear friend Umar” who “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding”.
In the post, signed by the couple, she said she and Trump Jr “got married privately on” 22 May “surrounded ONLY by our family”, and characterized the Russian businessman’s role in the post-wedding festivities as a gift.
“It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful,” she wrote, later adding: “Friendship doesn’t require a political motive. Generosity doesn’t automatically come with an agenda. And sometimes a wedding gift is simply a wedding gift.”

articles.title: Poland, Ukraine slam Russian strikes near border as 'escalation'
articles.body:
This handout picture taken and released by the Ukrainian State Emergency Service on September 13, 2026 shows firefighters spraying water at a train carriage damaged by a drone strike near the border with Poland. (AFP Photo)
The European Union’s top diplomat said on Sept. 14 that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine’s border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to “scare” off Kiev’s backers.
“It is clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support,” foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, urging Keiv’s backers to do “the opposite.”
Kallas’ remarks came a day after Poland and Ukraine denounced Russian strikes close to the Polish border that hit a Warsaw-bound train near a frontier checkpoint just after another train carrying several EU officials and British ex-PM Boris Johnson passed through.
Ukraine’s rail operator said Johnson and former CIA director David Petraeus, who were in Kiev for the annual Yalta European Strategy forum, had been traveling on two separate trains around the time the Warsaw-bound locomotive was hit on Sept. 13.
Petraeus told the New York Times in a telephone interview that he could hear Russian drones above followed by an explosion, prompting passengers to be quickly evacuated.
“For those who have not been under fire, this was terrifying. This is the act of a truly barbaric leader trying to terrorize Ukrainian civilians,” he added.
Johnson, who was traveling with several EU officials in a separate train, condemned the attack in a post on X.
“I don’t know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border,” he said.
“What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day, even on civilian railways.”
Poland and Ukraine said a Kiev-Warsaw passenger train was struck just two kilometers from the Polish border, but reported no casualties.
Warsaw has been one of Kiev’s main allies and, with Ukrainian airspace closed, trains to Poland have been one of the main routes out of the war-torn country, used by refugees.
The strikes came as U.S. President Donald Trump called on Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky to halt attacks on Russian refineries, saying it was causing a shortage of diesel fuel and “there are plenty of other targets.”
Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian oil refineries in a bid to hurt Russia’s war effort.
Zelensky said Moscow “deliberately” struck the locomotive.
“It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand,” Zelensky said.
Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk chaired an emergency meeting in Warsaw following the strikes, warning he expected Russia to escalate the war “in the coming weeks.”
Speaking in Kiev, Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said the “escalation” should lead to allies to “double” their support for Ukraine.

articles.title: ADF neutralizes 85 Russian drones overnight
articles.body:
ADF neutralizes 85 Russian drones overnight
According to Ukrinform, the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said this in a Telegram post.
Starting at 18:00 on September 13, Russia attacked Ukraine with 108 Shahed-type attack UAVs, including jet-powered ones, as well as Gerbera drones and Parody-type decoy drones launched from the directions of Orel and Kursk in Russia, temporarily occupied Donetsk, and Hvardiiske in temporarily occupied Crimea.
The air attack was repelled by aircraft, anti-aircraft missile forces, electronic warfare units, unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 08:00 on September 14, air defense forces had shot down or suppressed 85 drones.
Hits were recorded at seven locations. The attack is ongoing, and enemy UAVs remain in Ukrainian airspace.
As Ukrinform reported, Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 310 of the 323 drones used by Russia to attack Ukraine during the day on September 13.
Photo: Defense Forces

articles.title: Sybiha: Russia recruiting agents in Germany for surveillance, sabotage; Europe must step up its countermeasures
articles.body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha called on European governments to step up efforts to counter Russian influence and strengthen cooperation in the field of counterintelligence following an investigation by German RTL journalist Angelique Geray, which revealed the recruitment of agents in Germany to carry out surveillance and sabotage missions.
"I am impressed by the courage of the German investigative journalist from RTL, Angelique Geray, who worked undercover to expose Russia's secret recruitment network in Germany," Sybiha said on X social media platform.
According to him, the investigation found that agents were recruited via Telegram in exchange for money to carry out surveillance and sabotage missions. The undercover journalist was also threatened.
Sybiha said the RTL investigation is not an isolated case but points to a broader pattern of Russian sabotage operations in Europe.
"Putin invests heavily in destabilising Germany and other European nations, especially ahead of elections," the foreign minister said.
He also said Russia's goal is to interfere in the internal affairs of European countries, manipulate public opinion, and exploit the most sensitive and controversial issues.
Sybiha called on European governments to take this threat seriously, expose Russian influence, and take urgent measures – including addressing Russia's diplomatic and cultural presence, imposing sanctions against accomplices, banning Russian propaganda, and strengthening cooperation in the field of counterintelligence.
"As one of the most experienced nations in countering Russian influence, Ukraine is ready to share its valuable experience upon our partners' request," Sybiha said.

articles.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike in Sochi Wounds 5
articles.body:
Five people including a child were wounded in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the Black Sea resort city of Sochi, local officials said Monday.
Emergency authorities said only one of the victims was hospitalized for their injuries. Three homes were also damaged as a result of the air assault, they added.
Sochi Mayor Andrei Proshunin said firefighters extinguished fires that had broken out from the attack. He warned people not to approach any drone debris.
Proshunin later announced the closure of Sochis beache’s due to the ongoing risk of drone strikes.
In the neighboring Rostov region, Governor Yury Slyusar said air defense systems intercepted 50 drones over the region. He reported damage to civilian infrastructure but said that no one was hurt.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 399 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning.
Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a Russian attack on a farm warehouse in the northern Chernihiv region killed three people and injured seven others, police said Monday.
The deadly strike came after Russia struck a passenger train near Ukraine’s border with Poland on Sunday. A train carrying European officials was said to have passed through the area shortly before that attack.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Russia of trying to scare and divide Europeans.
Reuters contributed reporting.
A Message from The Moscow Times:

articles.title: Satellite images show 21 shelters at suspected Russian naval drone base at Lake Donuzlav in occupied Crimea
articles.body:
At least 21 protected shelters have been built on the shore of Lake Donuzlav in Russian-occupied Crimea. They are likely intended to protect Russian naval drones.
The suspected base was first identified by the Ukrainian open-source intelligence (OSINT) project CyberBoroshno, and naval researcher H. I. Sutton later analyzed satellite imagery of the site. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty’s project Krym.Realii highlighted their findings in a report on Sept. 4.
CyberBoroshno first reported the existence of the structures near Novoozerne on Sept. 1. The project’s analysts said the hangars were likely intended to store unmanned surface vessels (USVs) — remotely operated or autonomous boats.
The analysts said Russian forces have not yet been seen using these drones extensively in combat, but the construction of specialized infrastructure may indicate preparations for their future deployment. Using CyberBoroshno’s findings, H. I. Sutton examined satellite imagery of Donuzlav and counted at least 21 shelters at two sites along the lake’s southern shore.
According to his analysis, construction of the first eight shelters began in February 2026, while another eight appeared soon afterward. The second site was later expanded to 13 shelters. Roads are seen leading up to the shelters, allowing boats and equipment to be transported to the water. The shelters could be used to store, prepare, and launch the drones.
On Sept. 2, one day after CyberBoroshno published its findings, the Ukrainian Navy reported that it had destroyed a Russian Kama unmanned surface vessel near Snake Island. It is not currently known where the craft was launched from.
Russia officially unveiled the Kama for the first time in June 2026. According to its stated specifications, the vessel can operate up to 700 kilometers from its base and carry a payload of up to 600 kilograms.
Russia has already used naval drones in its war against Ukraine, but so far only in limited numbers, according to a source interviewed by Krym.Realii who previously served in Ukrainian military intelligence. The source said most of the military unmanned boats Russia has publicly displayed remain at the testing or prototype stage, with no evidence that they are being produced at scale.
In July, Russian Navy commander-in-chief Alexander Moiseyev announced the country was building its first 500-metric-ton unmanned vessel for hunting submarines and other underwater targets. The announcement drew criticism from several pro-war Russian Telegram channels and commentators, who argued that the Russian Navy should first establish mass production of small, inexpensive attack drones of the kind Ukraine has used extensively against Russian ships and infrastructure.

articles.title: Russia resumes mass launches of petrol-powered drones, threat of attack throughout the day
articles.body:
Russia resumes mass launches of petrol-powered drones, threat of attack throughout the day
The Air Force is warning of a threat of a massive attack by Russian strike drones throughout Monday 14 September, as the Russians are once again launching large numbers of UAVs powered by internal combustion engines.
Source: Colonel Yurii Ihnat, spokesperson for the Ukrainian Air Force, during the national joint 24/7 newscast
Quote: "We are currently observing an attack by enemy strike UAVs on Odesa Oblast. The threat also remains, of course, for the northern regions. There is information that the enemy may attack today from both the north and the east. That is to say, a large quantity of enemy UAVs is available to be launched towards our country. Specifically, these are UAVs with internal combustion engines, non-jet-powered...
At present, the enemy has clearly expended large stockpiles of jet drones, having attempted to use them for strikes as much as possible in August. A certain number of conventional, classic Shaheds have evidently been accumulated... They have now been launched in several waves, primarily targeting western regions, likely because jet-powered ones lack the range to fly such long distances. A balance must be struck there between fuel capacity, warhead size, and so on. It is expected that these attacks may continue throughout the day."
Details: Ihnat added that defenders of Ukrainian airspace are doing everything possible to minimise Russian hits (which are currently around 10%, compared to an approximate 90% interception rate).
He emphasised that all available assets and personnel within the layered, integrated air defence system have been deployed to repel Russian air attacks.
Asked by a journalist about the reason for this shift in Russian tactics – deploying petrol-powered Shaheds again instead of jet-powered ones – the Air Force spokesperson noted: "Let's assume that the enemy is always planning an unexpected operation to catch our air defence off guard somewhere, utilising various types of munitions. This includes various types of missiles – ballistic, cruise and air-launched – as well as strike UAVs... The enemy is using all means available."

articles.title: Winter could be turning point in war in Ukraine – Polish Defence Ministry
articles.body:
Winter could be turning point in war in Ukraine – Polish Defence Ministry
Polish Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk has said that Russian strikes near the Polish border are an attempt to cut Ukraine off from military supplies. He warned that the coming months, particularly the winter, could prove to be a turning point in the war, potentially in Russia's favour.
Source: Tomczyk in an interview with TVN24, as reported by European Pravda
Details: Tomczyk said that Russia believes the coming period could become a turning point in the war and that Ukraine currently needs the maximum possible support from the Western world to withstand Russia's war and effectively defend itself against aerial attacks.
According to Tomczyk, the recent attacks on Ukraine's west are also a test for NATO. He said that, according to CIA intelligence, Russia's plans for the near future include scenarios involving European countries.
Tomczyk said he did not want to disclose any sensational details but warned that the scenarios included possible acts of sabotage similar to those seen in Germany, a potential escalation of hybrid warfare on a scale not witnessed before, and various types of operations in border areas, including in the Baltic states along NATO's frontier. He said these were very realistic scenarios that could escalate into something far more serious.
Background:
- On 13 September, Russia struck the locomotive of a passenger train near the Polish border. Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) suggested that the Russian drone may have been targeting a train carrying diplomats and politicians, whose passengers had to be evacuated. Those on board included former UK prime minister Boris Johnson and Günter Sautter, one of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's closest advisers.
- Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that the coming weeks and months would be a period of very active Russian operations and that more serious attacks on Polish territory could not be ruled out.

articles.title: Five injured after Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Sochi
articles.body:
Five injured after Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Sochi
Ukraine’s military launched a drone attack on Krasnodar Krai overnight on September 14. In Sochi, the regional emergency response headquarters reported that five people, including a child, were injured by “falling drone debris”. One of the injured, an adult, was hospitalized, while the rest received outpatient care. Three private homes were damaged.
Rostov Governor Yuri Slyusar said air defenses shot down 50 drones over the region, including over Rostov-on-Don, Taganrog, and Aksai. He said there were no casualties, but “there’s damage on the ground,” adding that several cars, residential buildings, and power lines were damaged.
Russia’s Defense Ministry announced that air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 399 Ukrainian drones overnight.

articles.title: Ex-CIA Chief: Inside Putin’s Mafia State
articles.body:
Sean Wiswesser, a former CIA Chief of Station who spent decades working against Russian intelligence, says the image of the flawless Russian spy bears little resemblance to how the system actually works. The FSB, SVR and GRU are corrupt, often sloppy and still capable of penetrations, sabotage and assassinations abroad.
 “They remain formidable precisely because there’s no accountability,” he tells Kyiv Post special correspondent Jason Jay Smart.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Wiswesser traces that culture through the poisoning of Sergei Skripal, the assassination of Zelimkhan Khangoshvili in Berlin and Vladimir Putin’s successful effort to bring convicted assassin Vadim Krasikov back to Russia.
 Krasikov’s return sent its own message through the services: kill for the state and Moscow will fight to bring you home. Officers do not have to display perfect tradecraft when the system rewards aggression and rarely punishes failure.
 The criminal side of the FSB is even more direct.
 “They shake down the companies themselves! It’s very much like a mafia clan,” Wiswesser says of its Economic Security Service.
 He describes protection payments, cybercriminals working for Russian intelligence while continuing their own crimes, corruption inside intelligence training, and expendable recruits found through Telegram for arson and sabotage abroad. These are not invincible spies. They are dangerous because criminal methods and state power operate together.

articles.title: Russian Drone Strike Hits Kyiv-Warsaw Train Just 2 Kilometers From Polish Border
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russian Drone Strike Hits Kyiv-Warsaw Train Just 2 Kilometers From Polish Border
A Russian drone strike hit the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train in Ukraine’s Volyn region on September 13, approximately two kilometers from the Polish border.
According to state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia, no injuries were reported. Ukrzaliznytsia said a monitoring team had warned the train crew about the threat in advance.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The same Russian attack also struck infrastructure near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk international border crossing, one of the main road links between Ukraine and Poland.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reported the strike near the Yahodyn crossing on September 13. Valentyna Chernysh, a spokesperson for the Volyn Customs Service, told Suspilne that falling drone debris caused a fire at a nearby gas station and several trucks parked at the site.
Border operations were temporarily suspended during the air raid alert while personnel and other people at the crossing took shelter. The Yahodyn-Dorohusk checkpoint later resumed normal operations.
Sybiha said the strikes near the Polish border amounted to Putin’s terror “knocking” directly on the doors of the EU and NATO and called on Ukraine’s partners to impose broader sanctions on Russia.
“Act now: throw the full weight of your sanctions at Putin’s aggressive regime. Make Moscow feel the consequences of its terror. Not just half-decisions, but uncompromising, powerful steps. Full trade embargo. Full entry bans. Full sanctions on the military-industrial complex,” Sybiha wrote.
Earlier, on September 12, Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack across Ukraine, killing at least four people and injuring civilians in Odesa, Kryvyi Rih, Zaporizhzhia, and the Kyiv region.
Discuss this article:

articles.title: Russian forces launch Kalibr missiles without sending launch vessels to sea — Navy
articles.body:
Russian forces launch Kalibr missiles without sending launch vessels to sea — Navy
Dmytro Pletenchuk, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian Navy, made this statement during a television broadcast, according to Ukrinform.
“Even the launch of cruise missile carriers that fire ‘Kalibrs’ is taking place directly at their base, that is, right in the harbor. This is a trend that has been observed for the fourth consecutive month,” Pletenchuk noted.
He noted that the Russians use cruise missiles relatively rarely. According to him, there have been two such launches this month, and over the summer, the maximum number of launches was three.
Pletenchuk noted that Russia potentially has up to four vessels capable of launching cruise missiles from the Black Sea: two “Buyan-M” class surface ships and two “Varshavyanka” class submarines.
“Submarines, for example, aren’t that easy to deploy either. To do so, they need to submerge. I still can’t imagine how they could use them in exactly the same way they’re currently carrying out launches. Let’s not downplay the danger: we’re assuming the maximum—four launch platforms—but a more realistic figure would probably be two surface vessels,” Pletenchuk said.
As reported, the Air Defense Forces neutralized 85 out of 108 drones used by Russian invaders to attack Ukraine beginning on the evening of September 13.
Illustrative photo: Air Force

articles.title: Russia Recruits More Than 28,000 Foreign Nationals for War in Ukraine
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russia Recruits More Than 28,000 Foreign Nationals for War in Ukraine
Russia has recruited more than 28,000 foreign nationals to join its war against Ukraine, including a substantial number of people from African countries, according to Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence (HUR) chief Oleh Ivashchenko.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
In an interview with The Times, Ivashchenko said Ukrainian intelligence is working to disrupt Moscow’s efforts to recruit fighters abroad.
“We’re working to stop this, by passing information to the relevant security and intelligence services. We also conduct non-kinetic operations to inform the population in the relevant countries,” Ivashchenko said.
Beyond recruiting foreign nationals, Russia continues to receive military assistance from North Korea. HUR estimates that approximately 8,000 North Korean troops are currently deployed in Russia’s Kursk region, with their number potentially rising to around 50,000.
Russia’s reliance on foreign manpower extends across multiple regions. In an earlier interview with Ukrinform on September 7, Ivashchenko said Moscow was recruiting nationals from more than 40 countries as it seeks both to replenish battlefield losses and expand its forces for potential future military objectives.
“Today, Russia is using foreign nationals from more than 40 countries, including countries in Central Asia, Africa, and Latin America. They are primarily deployed in assault units. In intercepted communications, the Russians themselves call them ‘allies’ and often send them ahead of their own troops,” he stated.
Overall, Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry estimates that Russia has recruited at least 2,982 nationals from 37 African countries into its armed forces, with approximately 486 reportedly killed in the war against Ukraine.
Discuss this article:

articles.title: Trump downplays report China entities helped Iran before attack
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Trump downplays report China entities helped Iran before attack that killed US troops
US President Donald Trump on Sunday brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.
A recent report in the Wall Street Journal cited unnamed US officials about the attack in Jordan. Asked whether he would mention the issue at an upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Trump did not directly answer, and instead equated the surveillance activities of China and the United States.
"They basically do what we do," he told reporters aboard Air Force One. "When they say China spies on us, I say you're right and we spy on them too."
The Chinese and US presidents are expected to meet in the United States on 24 September, although China has yet to officially confirm that the meeting will take place.
Trump on Sunday reiterated his view that he has a good relationship with Xi.
"I think he's behaved reasonably well, and we behave reasonably well," Trump said as he flew back to the United States after a weekend trip to Ireland.
The Wall Street Journal report, which Reuters could not immediately verify, said the US officials declined to identify the Chinese entities that supplied the imagery to Iran and did not allege direct involvement by Beijing.
Trump's comments appeared consistent with the administration's recent efforts to play down wide-ranging tensions between Washington and Beijing, despite US frustration over Beijing's close ties to Tehran.
At least 18 US service personnel have been killed and hundreds injured since the US-Israeli war with Iran began at the end of February.

articles.title: US wants to resume talks on Iran's nuclear program
articles.body:
The US wants to resume talks on Tehran’s nuclear program in its talks with Iran, CNN reported.
According to the TV channel, officials from US President Donald Trump’s administration have indicated in private conversations with representatives of Persian Gulf states that Washington would like to "refocus any future US-Iran negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear program and not reopening the Strait [of Hormuz]."
For their part, Iranian representatives have made it clear to regional players that they will only be open to discussing their nuclear program after the Strait of Hormuz issue is resolved, including the lifting of the US blockade of Iranian seaports.
The US and the Israeli regime launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran, with Islamabad acting as mediator, signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, in the early morning hours of July 8, the US resumed large-scale strikes against Iran.

articles.title: Russia Could Be Preparing Serious Strikes on Poland in Coming Weeks and Months, Tusk Warns

Russia Could Be Preparing Serious Strikes on Poland in Coming Weeks and Months, Tusk Warns
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia’s escalating actions could increasingly affect Poland in the coming weeks and months, as Moscow intensifies attacks near the country’s borders.
Speaking at a briefing at Poland’s Government Security Center on September 13, Tusk said recent developments showed that Russian escalation was becoming increasingly apparent and moving closer to Polish territory, according to Polish broadcaster RMF24.

“Russia’s escalation is becoming a reality, and examples of it are getting closer and closer to our border,” Tusk said. “We must be prepared for a joint response if necessary.”c
Tusk also pointed to Russia’s latest attacks on Ukraine as evidence that Moscow is deploying increasingly dangerous weapons, specifically highlighting the growing use of jet-powered drones.
“The attacks last night demonstrate that the Russians are ready to use more dangerous equipment. I mean jet-powered drones […] Obviously, Ukraine, which is very well prepared to defend against drones, is also unable to counter them with 100% effectiveness,” he said.
Polish Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk, who also attended the briefing, said 13 strikes were recorded in western regions of Ukraine during the Russian drone attack on September 13.
Against this backdrop, Tusk called for an assessment of Poland’s readiness to respond to potential drone-related threats, including operations that could disrupt critical infrastructure and transportation networks.
“I will therefore also be waiting for information on how prepared we are for the possible use of drones and related attempts to disrupt our operations, on the railway or elsewhere. I do not rule out that such situations could also occur here,” Tusk said.
His warning came as the September 13 Russian attack reached areas immediately bordering Poland. A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train in Ukraine’s Volyn region, approximately two kilometers from the Polish border.
State railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia reported that no one was injured, adding that a monitoring team had warned the train crew of the threat in advance.
The same attack also damaged infrastructure near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk international border crossing, one of the main road connections between Ukraine and Poland.
